tagline: One of Islam's most sacred sites outside Arabia — the Eyüp Sultan Mosque, Pierre Loti Hill, and the Golden Horn waterfront in a deeply spiritual setting.

items.name: Pierre Loti Çay Bahçesi
items.description: A legendary hilltop tea garden above Eyüpsultan with sweeping Golden Horn views. Reached by cable car from the cemetery. One of Istanbul's most atmospheric spots.
items.tip: Take the teleferik (cable car) up and walk back down through the Ottoman cemetery. The views from the top are extraordinary.

items.name: Eyüpsultan Çarşısı
items.description: The bazaar streets around the mosque have traditional food stalls and lokanta restaurants serving simple, honest Turkish food.

items.name: Eyüp Sultan Camii
items.description: One of the holiest mosques in Istanbul — built over the tomb of Eyüp el-Ensari, a companion of the Prophet. A place of genuine pilgrimage and reverence.
items.tip: Dress very modestly — this is an active place of worship, not a tourist attraction. Visit with respect and quiet.

items.name: Pierre Loti Tepesi
items.description: The hill above Eyüpsultan named after the French novelist who frequented the café here. Golden Horn panorama and historic Ottoman cemetery.

items.name: Eyüpsultan Türbesi ve Tarihi Mezarlık
items.description: The historic Ottoman cemetery surrounding the mosque is one of the most atmospheric in Istanbul — centuries of marble tombstones among cypress trees.

tips: Eyüpsultan is reached by bus from Taksim or Eminönü, or by the Golden Horn ferry (Haliç İskelesi).
Dress conservatively — this is one of Istanbul's most religiously significant neighbourhoods.
Combine with Fener and Balat (20 minutes by bus) for a full day on the Golden Horn.
The cable car (teleferik) to Pierre Loti runs from the edge of the cemetery — short and scenic.
